newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka MP, guard dead in campaign shooting.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka MP, guard dead in campaign shooting.

text.p: Unknown assailants shot and killed a member of parliament from the ruling People's Alliance in southern Sri Lanka on Tuesday, police said.
Lawmaker Nalanda Ellawala was shot in the stomach and died in hospital.

The assailants also killed the bodyguard of another ruling party legislator and injured five others in the shooting, which occurred when Ellawala and his backers encountered opposition supporters on a road in Kuruwita, 80 km (50 miles) south of Colombo, police said.
Both groups were on the road canvassing the predominantly farming and rubber-growing area before key local elections scheduled for next month. Wednesday is the deadline for submitting nominations.
Ellawala, 29, was taken to a local hospital but died on the operating table, police said.
Police said they have made no arrests and have imposed a curfew for the Ratnapura district, where Kuruwita is located.
The shooting took place when Ellawala's procession was blocked by a group of activists from the main opposition United National Party (UNP).
"Ellawala was proceeding to Colombo when their way was blocked by the UNP procession," a police official in Kuruwita said.
"He got down from his vehicle and an argument ensued. His bodyguards then fired into the air. It was then that somebody shot at them," the Kuruwita police official said.
The official said police were investigating the shooting but had no further details. They said it was not clear who actually fired the shots.
The UNP activists had just handed in their nominations for the local polls, tentatively scheduled for March 27.
The elections are the first test for President Chandrika Kumaratunga's government, which ended 17 years of UNP rule by winning general and presidential elections in 1994.
A spokesman for the People's Alliance condemned the shooting.
"This is another attempt to restart terror tactics in politics," the spokesman said in a broadcast on state radio Sri Lanka Broadcasting Corporation soon after the shooting.
A UNP lawmaker denied his party was trying to foment election violence.
"Our party has vehemently told our supporters that under no circumstances must they practice violence in this election," UNP member of parliament Jayalath Jayawardana told Reuters.
"The UNP will not get involved in such activity," Jayawardana said.

Sri Lanka has a history of election violence. UNP presidential candidate Gamini Dissanayake was assassinated by a suspected suicide bomber of the separatist Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) in November 1994.
The LTTE is fighting for a separate homeland in Sri Lanka's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the conflict since 1983 but the LTTE says the toll is much higher.
